body.en: "On the Face of It" is a short play by the English writer Susan Hill. It has two scenes: the first in Mr Lamb's large, open garden and the second at Derry's home. The title suggests looking only at the surface of things, and the play asks us to look deeper than faces.

title.en: Character map: On the Face of It

narration.en: We map the three characters of the play and how they connect.

say.en: At the centre is Derry, a boy with a burnt face.
Mr Lamb is old, has a tin leg and keeps his gate open.
Derry's mother protects him and distrusts Mr Lamb.
The local children tease Mr Lamb with a nickname.
Strangers stare at Derry with pity or fear.
The garden, with bees and apples, brings them together.

right.en: A boy of about fourteen, his face burnt by acid
An old man with a tin leg who keeps his gate open
Protective and distrustful of Mr Lamb

explanation.en: Two people hurt by how others see them meet, and one changes the other.

body.en: Derry, about fourteen, has one side of his face badly burnt by acid. He is bitter, shy and keeps away from people because of how they react. Mr Lamb is an old man with a tin leg, having lost a leg in the war. He lives alone but keeps his garden gate open to everyone and is cheerful and welcoming. Derry's mother is protective and distrusts Mr Lamb.

points.en: Mr Lamb: old, tin leg, cheerful

narration.en: Derry, about fourteen, has one side of his face badly burnt by acid. He is bitter, shy and keeps away from people because of how they react. Mr Lamb is an old man with a tin leg, having lost a leg in the war. He lives alone but keeps his garden gate open to everyone and is cheerful and welcoming. Derry's mother is protective and distrusts Mr Lamb.

problem.en: How are Derry and Mr Lamb alike, and how are they different?

steps.en: Alike: both have a physical disability and both are outsiders.
Different: Derry is bitter and withdrawn.
Mr Lamb is cheerful and open to the world.

answer.en: Both Derry and Mr Lamb have physical disabilities and are treated as outsiders. But Derry reacts with bitterness and withdraws from people, while Mr Lamb accepts his tin leg, stays cheerful and keeps his gate open to everyone.

narration.en: Let us build a model answer together. How are Derry and Mr Lamb alike, and how are they different?

body.en: Remember Mr Lamb by three L's: his Leg of tin, the Lonely life he lives without self-pity, and the Lessons he gives Derry.
